item.title: Bangladesh Cuts India Visa Services While Sri Lanka, Nepal Court Its Travelers
item.description: The world may be looking to get more Indian travelers, but not every country is keen on it, even if India is a low-hanging fruit sitting right beside it.

item.title: India Is Losing Tourism Dollars, Even as Domestic Travel Is Booming
item.description: India's current tourism revenue makes one thing crystal clear: Just talking about the importance of tourism without an actionable strategy is a short-sighted move, and the country doesn't seem to get beyond rhetoric.

item.title: Hilton Debuts Apartment Collection as 26th Brand
item.description: Hilton’s new brand is a long-delayed acknowledgment that a certain type of traveler wants the space of a residential apartment along with the consistency, on-site staff, and loyalty points of a hotel.

item.title: Why Lemon Tree Is Spinning Off Its Hotels Into a New Company
item.description: Moral of the story: companies don’t have to own hotels to run them well anymore.

item.title: Travel’s Wallet Share Reckoning Is Here
item.description: Travel's share of consumer wallets shows spending has returned to normal. The binge is over.

item.title: Mamdani Takes on Junk Fees in NYC: Where it Stands and What it Could Mean for Travel
item.description: New York City's move signals growing local-government appetite to go beyond federal standards.

item.title: Greenland Tourism’s Trump Problem: Surviving the Unwanted Spotlight
item.description: For a remote destination selling silence and sustainability, geopolitical attention may prove harder to manage than rapid tourism growth.

item.title: AI Growth Is Driving Up U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions – What Travel Businesses Need to Know
item.description: While AI may help find ways to cut emissions, ignoring its own growing footprint could impact the travel industry's climate goals.

item.title: Delta’s Next Multi-Billion-Dollar Business You Haven’t Heard of
item.description: As Delta executives remain cautiously optimistic about 2026, they're revealing more details about one it's most lucrative businesses: maintenance, repair, and overhaul. Delta expects revenues from the unit to eventually top $3 billion.

item.title: The Thrill Is Gone: Airbnb and the Crisis of Imagination in Short-Term Rentals
item.description: Airbnb’s struggle to translate technology into better stays mirrors the broader sector’s problem — digital scale without physical control limits how innovative short-term rentals can be.
